python_only.CODEX_SOCKET_MODULE: Python loads the codex module by path, since it imports asyncssh, so a server without the ssh extra starts; TypeScript's codex module only types ssh2 and is imported directly.
python_only.TUNNEL_CHUNK: Python's route reads the SSH server's side of a socket pair in chunks; TypeScript pipes a ws stream, which chunks for itself.
python_only.TUNNEL_MODULE: Python loads asyncssh's module by path, so a server without the ssh extra starts; TypeScript imports the module dynamically by its literal path.

python_only.pump: websockets reads a connection as an async iterator, so Python carries each direction through one function; ws hands TypeScript each message to an event handler.

typescript_only.Admit: ssh2 takes a login decision as a callback, typed here; asyncssh asks a server object (MirageSSHServer, TunnelSSHServer).
typescript_only.admitTunnel: ssh2 admits a tunneled login through a callback; asyncssh's twin is the TunnelSSHServer class in session.

python_only.TunnelSSHServer: asyncssh admits a login through a server object, and key_account reads the tunnel's account off it; ssh2's twin is the admitTunnel callback in server.

python_only.SSHTunnel: Python types the connection its lazily loaded tunnel returns; TypeScript's serveTunnel resolves when the connection ends.
python_only.ServeCodexSocket: Python types serve_codex_socket for the route that loads it by path; TypeScript imports it directly.
python_only.ServeTunnel: Python types serve_tunnel for the route that loads it by path; TypeScript imports it and keeps its own signature.

python_only.login_cmd: Typer commands are module functions; commander registers the same command inline in registerLoginCommands.
python_only.logout_cmd: Typer commands are module functions; commander registers the same command inline in registerLoginCommands.
python_only.whoami_cmd: Typer commands are module functions; commander registers the same command inline in registerLoginCommands.
python_only.QuietHandler: Python's http.server serves through a handler class, whose access log is silenced here; Node's createServer takes the handler as a function and logs nothing.

typescript_only.registerLoginCommands: commander registers commands through a function; Typer's are the module functions login_cmd, logout_cmd and whoami_cmd.

python_only.protected_resource: FastAPI routes are module functions; Fastify registers the same handler inline in registerOAuthRoutes.

typescript_only.OAuthDeps: Fastify routes take their dependencies as an object; FastAPI routes read them off app.state.
typescript_only.registerOAuthRoutes: Fastify registers routes through a function; FastAPI's route is the module function protected_resource.

typescript_only.CacheConfigSchema: Python checks the config through its pydantic model, which forbids extra fields; a TypeScript config is a plain object, so the code entry point parses it with this schema through parseConfigWithSchema.
typescript_only.RedisCacheConfigSchema: Python checks the config through its pydantic model, which forbids extra fields; a TypeScript config is a plain object, so the code entry point parses it with this schema through parseConfigWithSchema.
typescript_only.normalizeCacheConfig: Python checks the config when the model is built; a TypeScript config is a plain object, so the Workspace checks it here, through parseConfigWithSchema, when it is built.

typescript_only.IndexConfigSchema: Python checks the config through its pydantic model, which forbids extra fields; a TypeScript config is a plain object, so the code entry point parses it with this schema through parseConfigWithSchema.
typescript_only.RedisIndexConfigSchema: Python checks the config through its pydantic model, which forbids extra fields; a TypeScript config is a plain object, so the code entry point parses it with this schema through parseConfigWithSchema.
typescript_only.normalizeIndexConfig: Python checks the config when the model is built; a TypeScript config is a plain object, so the Workspace checks it here, through parseConfigWithSchema, when it is built.
typescript_only.FileStatWireSchema: pydantic validates a stat row Python reads back; TypeScript parses one with this schema.

python_only._PREFIX_LOCK: Python runs event loops on several threads, so the shared per-prefix write and holder counts take a lock; TypeScript runs one thread.

python_only._counts_listing_write: Python counts a store method's listing write with this decorator, so the method body stays as it is; TypeScript has no method decorators here and wraps the body in ListingMemo.writing.

typescript_only.refuseRepeatedFields: Python's models take one spelling of a field, so a second spelling is an extra field pydantic refuses; a TypeScript config takes either spelling, so the code entry point refuses one field named in both.

python_only._YamlLoader: PyYAML needs a SafeLoader subclass to recognize exponent-only floats without changing yaml.safe_load globally; TypeScript's yaml package already uses YAML 1.2 exponent resolution. Both loaders read the shared YAML scalar fixture.

typescript_only.mod7: JavaScript's % keeps the dividend's sign, so the weekday arithmetic needs a helper for a remainder from 0 to 6; Python's % already gives one.
typescript_only.EXACT: Python's integers are exact at any size; TypeScript sums relative counts as BigInt and needs the bound past which a total no longer converts to a double exactly.

python_only.RedisWorkspaceStateStore: Python's optional imports bind a class or None; explicit annotations expose these existing bindings to the symbol checker.
python_only.S3WorkspaceStateStore: Python's optional imports bind a class or None; explicit annotations expose these existing bindings to the symbol checker.

typescript_only.validateIndexValues: Python checks an index block's values through its pydantic models (str url and key_prefix, StrictFloat ttl); the TypeScript loader has no model for the block, so it checks the values by hand at the same entry point.

python_only.document: Python uses decorated Typer/FastAPI handlers and request models; TypeScript registers matching routes and commands as closures with typed inputs. Cross-host document and session behavior is covered by integ/access.
python_only._register: FastAPI routes are added per document on the module router; Fastify registers the same GET and PUT routes in registerDocumentsRoutes. Cross-host document and session behavior is covered by integ/access.

typescript_only.DocumentParams: Python uses decorated Typer/FastAPI handlers and request models; TypeScript registers matching routes and commands as closures with typed inputs. Cross-host document and session behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.DocumentQuery: Python uses decorated Typer/FastAPI handlers and request models; TypeScript registers matching routes and commands as closures with typed inputs. Cross-host document and session behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.DocumentsRoutesDeps: Python uses decorated Typer/FastAPI handlers and request models; TypeScript registers matching routes and commands as closures with typed inputs. Cross-host document and session behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.registerDocumentsRoutes: Python uses decorated Typer/FastAPI handlers and request models; TypeScript registers matching routes and commands as closures with typed inputs. Cross-host document and session behavior is covered by integ/access.

typescript_only.BoxFileInfo: The shape of GET /files/{id} with the fields the fresh check asks for (path_collection, item_status) beside BoxItem's; Python reads the same answer as a plain dict, as it does every Box item.

typescript_only.Scope: explainedLine groups judgments by the scope they were evaluated from; Python keys a dict by (parent occurrence, text), which needs no named shape.
typescript_only.sameAt: Occurrences compare by reference in TypeScript, so finding a scope compares them field by field; Python's frozen dataclass equality does it.

python_only.set_current_evaluation: Python binds an evaluation with its session and returns the ContextVar token reset_current_session restores; TypeScript runWithEvaluation scopes the binding around an async callback.

typescript_only.CallerDispatchFn: TypeScript's DispatchFn lives in the runtime types, which import no workspace module and so cannot name the Caller; the dispatcher and the workspace functions that hand it a caller take this type. Python's DispatchFn carries the caller through its keywords.
typescript_only.runWithEvaluation: TypeScript scopes the evaluation's session binding around a callback; Python set_current_evaluation returns a ContextVar token.
typescript_only.callerSignal: TypeScript hands the current call's AbortSignal to a read or copy of a live pipe, so a reader that gives up (timeout) withdraws its claim on the pipe; Python cancels the awaiting task, which the pipe's shielded pull answers directly.
typescript_only.lineSignal: TypeScript must pass a line's AbortSignal into fetch to interrupt an outstanding response body read; Python task cancellation interrupts the awaited HTTP read directly.

python_only.app: Typer registers one function per command and holds the group in a module-level `app`; the TypeScript CLI builds the same commands on a commander program inside its register function.
python_only.glob_cmd: Typer registers one function per command and holds the group in a module-level `app`; the TypeScript CLI builds the same commands on a commander program inside its register function.
python_only.EXPLAIN: Typer reads a command's options off its function signature, so the generated commands are built from shared Option values and an inspect.Parameter per argument; commander adds each option to the command directly.
python_only.SESSION: Typer reads a command's options off its function signature, so the generated commands are built from shared Option values and an inspect.Parameter per argument; commander adds each option to the command directly.
python_only.WORKSPACE: Typer reads a command's options off its function signature, so the generated commands are built from shared Option values and an inspect.Parameter per argument; commander adds each option to the command directly.
python_only._parameter: Typer reads a command's options off its function signature, so the generated commands are built from shared Option values and an inspect.Parameter per argument; commander adds each option to the command directly.

typescript_only.registerVfsCommands: Typer registers one function per command and holds the group in a module-level `app`; the TypeScript CLI builds the same commands on a commander program inside its register function.
typescript_only.Target: Commander hands an action its options as one camelCased object, which TypeScript types as Target and maps back to the call's snake_case argument names; Typer passes each option as its own keyword argument.
typescript_only.camel: Commander hands an action its options as one camelCased object, which TypeScript types as Target and maps back to the call's snake_case argument names; Typer passes each option as its own keyword argument.

python_only.glob: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
python_only.router: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
python_only.vfs_route: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
python_only.json_body: FastAPI hands a route the raw request, so the VFS, glob and tool routes read their JSON object through json_body, bounded by MCP's size limit; Fastify parses and bounds the body itself (bodyLimit).
python_only.streamed_read: FastAPI has module-level route handlers; the matching Fastify handler streams a read inline in registerVfsRoutes.
python_only.custom_function: FastAPI has module-level route handlers; the matching Fastify handler is a closure in registerVfsRoutes.

typescript_only.CallQuery: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.RouteError: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.VfsRoutesDeps: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.queryFlag: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.
typescript_only.registerVfsRoutes: FastAPI routes are module-level handlers on a router; Fastify registers the same routes as closures in registerVfsRoutes, with typed query and error shapes. Cross-host behavior is covered by integ/access.

typescript_only.attrs: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.
typescript_only.bin: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.
typescript_only.flag: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.
typescript_only.int: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.
typescript_only.nofollow: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.
typescript_only.str: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.
typescript_only.row: TypeScript methods take positional arguments and option objects, so each row's run reads its arguments off the checked record through typed accessors and is built with row(); Python calls the method of the same name with the arguments by keyword.

python_only.DaemonMcpServer: A Python Session call runs on the workspace runner's loop, so the daemon serves MCP with a subclass whose hop does it, as DaemonRpcServer does for RPC; TypeScript has one loop and hands its tool table to createMirageMcpServer.

typescript_only.raw: isomorphic-git hands back a parsed object, so TypeScript reads the stored bytes in a helper; dulwich's as_raw_string gives them in Python.

python_only.OBJECT_CLASSES: dulwich stores an object built from its class; isomorphic-git's writeObject takes the type name, so TypeScript needs no table.
python_only.TREE_ENTRY: Python matches a tree entry with a bytes regex; TypeScript walks the latin-1 text by index in wellFormed.

typescript_only.Parsed: The headers and message a parse of an object holds; Python's _headers returns them as a tuple.
typescript_only.PARSED: TypeScript keeps each object's parse in a WeakMap, since its fields decode the bytes once; Python's _headers splits the text again per call.
typescript_only.field: Builds the RefField record Python's dataclass constructor builds with its defaults.
typescript_only.value: Builds the FieldValue record Python's dataclass constructor builds.
typescript_only.withField: Copies a RefField with changes, as Python's dataclasses.replace does.

python_only._order: Python compares two strings by code point as a -1/0/1; TypeScript imports compareCodePoints.

python_only.OBJECT_TYPES: dulwich's get_raw names an object's type by its pack number; TypeScript's object reader hands back the type name.

python_only._endpoint: Python reads the endpoint through the EndpointVFS protocol (S3VFS.resolved_endpoint); TypeScript asks `vfs instanceof S3VFSBase` and reads its resolvedEndpoint getter.

typescript_only.WriteDefaults: Python's normalize_mounts takes the write default, mode and caching as keyword arguments; TypeScript's positional signature takes them as one options object.

python_only.own_write_version: Python binds per-call context by setting and restoring its caller ContextVar; TypeScript runs a callback in a scoped async-context store (runWithCacheManager and storage). The write context and the op's own version follow that same split.
python_only._own_version_for: Python keeps the op's own version in one ContextVar paired with its path and reads it here; TypeScript filters its live async-context frames by path inside ownVersion, which Python's _own_version pairs with.

typescript_only.activeWriteContext: TypeScript binds per-call context by running a callback in a scoped async-context store, as runWithCacheManager does; Python sets and restores a ContextVar instead. The write context and the op's own version follow that same split.
typescript_only.runWithOwnVersion: TypeScript binds per-call context by running a callback in a scoped async-context store, as runWithCacheManager does; Python sets and restores a ContextVar instead. The write context and the op's own version follow that same split.
typescript_only.runWithWriteContext: TypeScript binds per-call context by running a callback in a scoped async-context store, as runWithCacheManager does; Python sets and restores a ContextVar instead. The write context and the op's own version follow that same split.
typescript_only.agree: TypeScript's fallback async-context storage can hold several live frames that disagree on the write context or the op's own version; Python's ContextVar is always task-isolated, so there is nothing to agree.
typescript_only.overlapping: TypeScript's fallback async-context storage can hold several live frames that disagree on the write context or the op's own version; Python's ContextVar is always task-isolated, so there is nothing to agree.
typescript_only.ownersOf: TypeScript's fallback async-context storage can hold live frames of several overlapping lines at once, so a path is answered by the frames of the longest prefix covering it; Python's ContextVar is always task-isolated, so its one frame is the owner.

python_only.active_lost: The running line's lost paths ride Python's Recorder, which is still bound when apply_io runs, so the dispatcher reads them from the context. TypeScript applies a line's results after its recording scope ends, so it keys them by the line's records instead (lostPaths/lostByLine).
python_only.fresh_recorder: Python's recorder is a frozen Recorder that carries the line's lost paths and version index, built in one place for a line and for a file call outside one; TypeScript's recording is a plain records array and mount id, made where it is needed.

typescript_only.lostPaths: TypeScript retrieves a line's lost paths by its records array after its recording scope ends; Python reads the current Recorder through active_lost. This function was previously folded with the LostPaths class, now moved to observe/record on both hosts.
typescript_only.lostByLine: TypeScript keys a line's lost paths by its records array, because applyIo runs after runWithRecording returns; Python keeps them on the Recorder (active_lost).
typescript_only.recordIndex: TypeScript keys a line's version index by its records array, as it does the line's lost paths (lostPaths); Python keeps the index on the Recorder (Recorder.index), which push_mount_context carries.
typescript_only.indexByLine: The WeakMap behind recordIndex, keyed by a line's records array; Python keeps the index on the Recorder (Recorder.index).

typescript_only.isMissingBucket: TypeScript's isNotFoundError counts any 404, so lostCondition excludes a missing bucket by name; Python's _key_gone reads the same rule off the botocore response.

typescript_only.savedName: Python spells a saved policy with str() inline; TypeScript narrows the unknown JSON value before String(), which the lint requires, in one helper.

typescript_only.isStaleWrite: TypeScript errors are FsError objects tagged by code, so a stale write is read through a type guard, as isEfbig reads EFBIG; Python catches StaleWriteError by class.
typescript_only.isLandedMove: TypeScript errors are FsError objects tagged by field, so a landed move is read through a type guard, as isDotWalkError reads dotWalk; Python reads StaleWriteError.landed off the class.
typescript_only.unnamedFsError: TypeScript tags a code onto an Error that names no path (S3's DeleteObjects refusal names a key, not a path); Python raises the built-in PermissionError without a filename.

python_only.numbered: pathlib reads an OSError's errno to tell a missing path from a broken one, so the Python file adapter renumbers an error a third-party mount raised without one; a TypeScript error carries its code, which is what node callers read.

python_only.check_unlink: Python binds the check to a registry with functools.partial (make_check_unlink), as it does storage_key; TypeScript's makeCheckUnlink returns a closure, so the unbound function has no twin.

python_only.CheckFn: Python names the PrimitiveMove.check_unlink callable type beside MoveFn, as a forward reference to PathSpec; TypeScript types the field inline.

typescript_only.DirListingInit: A TypeScript DirListing takes its fields as one object; the Python dataclass takes them as keywords.
typescript_only.LIMIT_FIELDS: Limit.layered walks every field in order; Python reads them off the pydantic model's model_fields, a TypeScript class has no field list to walk.

typescript_only.VERSION_SHA: node-redis has no registered-script object for a pipeline, so TypeScript hashes version.lua itself, sends EVALSHA, and loads the script again when the server answers NOSCRIPT; redis-py's register_script does both.
typescript_only.noScript: node-redis has no registered-script object for a pipeline, so TypeScript hashes version.lua itself, sends EVALSHA, and loads the script again when the server answers NOSCRIPT; redis-py's register_script does both.

python_only._text: redis-py returns a stored version as bytes or str depending on decode_responses; node-redis returns a string, so TypeScript has nothing to decode.

typescript_only.requireHook: Python narrows a conditional op's *_if hook with assert; TypeScript's lint bans the non-null assertion, so the narrowing is this helper.

typescript_only.LostOptions: Python takes a refusal's landed, gone, versions and error as keyword arguments; TypeScript names them in one options object, so swapped booleans cannot type-check.

python_only.EndpointVFS: Python asks an S3 mount for its endpoint through this runtime-checkable protocol, since importing the S3 VFS would load its optional extra; TypeScript asks `vfs instanceof S3VFSBase`, which core always carries.

typescript_only.Handed: Python hands the stats as keyword arguments a backend function declares; TypeScript has no keyword arguments, so they ride in one object.

python_only.is_key_gone: Python reads a conditioned request's 404 off the botocore response (status and code) beside is_not_found; TypeScript composes isNotFoundError with isMissingBucket inline in the driver's lostCondition.

typescript_only.workspaceBridge: The TypeScript guest bridge takes fixed op names, string paths and positional payloads because those cross the Pyodide worker's postMessage, where a PathSpec does not survive structured clone, and they carry the xattr ops RuntimeFiles has no method for; one converter maps them onto the workspace dispatch. Python's RuntimeFiles calls DispatchFn in process with keyword arguments, so there is nothing to convert.

python_only.DECODERS: Python's codecs go by their own names and a few differ from the standard's (GBK decodes as gb18030); TextDecoder takes the WHATWG name itself.

python_only.atime_ns: Nanoseconds in python and milliseconds in TypeScript, as mtime_ns and mtimeMs: epoch nanoseconds are past 2**53, so a JS number cannot hold them exactly, while a python int can and preview1 asks in them.

typescript_only.atimeMs: Nanoseconds in python and milliseconds in TypeScript, as mtime_ns and mtimeMs: epoch nanoseconds are past 2**53, so a JS number cannot hold them exactly, while a python int can and preview1 asks in them.

typescript_only.LOCAL_CONFIG_KEYS: A TypeScript config interface lists its keys so an unknown one fails loud at construction; Python's dataclass refuses an unknown field by itself (RuntimeConfig.coerce).

typescript_only.isExecutable: Checks that the program found on PATH is an executable file; Python's shutil.which already checks that.

typescript_only.runtimeUnavailable: A TypeScript engine (Pyodide, Monty, QuickJS) can find it cannot run only when a run starts, and says so with its own error, which the interpreter and a script CLI both answer with 127; a Python entry that cannot run fails to build and is left out of the world, so no run raises it.

python_only._text_lines: Reads the text lines of an IMAPResponse from mirage's own Python IMAP client (accessor/imap); node's imapflow hands back parsed messages, so its client has no lines to read.

typescript_only.CLIHandlerInit: TypeScript describes constructor keyword objects with an interface; Python declares those fields on the CLIHandler dataclass.
typescript_only.CLIInit: TypeScript describes constructor keyword objects with an interface; Python declares those fields on the CLI dataclass.

typescript_only.ArgumentInit: TypeScript describes the Argument constructor options with an interface; Python spells them as constructor keyword parameters.

typescript_only.PARSES: TypeScript keeps each spec's readings in a WeakMap keyed by the spec, as compileSpec keeps its tables; Python keeps them on the spec itself, since a frozen dataclass key would hash every field on every parse.

typescript_only.deadlineCheck: A JavaScript generator cannot be cancelled from outside, so a TypeScript scan inside one pull checks the invocation's deadline itself; Python's with_timeout cancels the pull, and the scan stops at its next await.

python_only.LATE_WALL: A Python datetime holds no year past 9999, so from 9990 on a zone is read 400 years earlier for the standard-time search; a JavaScript Date holds those years.
python_only.HOST_STRETCHES: Python reads a host zone it cannot name through time.localtime, which gives no tzinfo to key a weak map by, so those stretches are kept under the host's zone names; TypeScript keys every zone, LOCAL_ZONE included, in one WeakMap.

typescript_only.HOST_ZONES: The host's zone per name Intl gives it, each read through one formatter; Python names the host's zone through its TZ or /etc/localtime and keeps it with functools.cache.
typescript_only.longNames: Builds the one Intl formatter per zone that reads its long name; Python's tzinfo answers dst() with no formatter.
typescript_only.offsetAt: Reads the host's offset from Date, which needs no formatter, and any other zone's from its parts; Python's tzinfo answers utcoffset() for every zone.
typescript_only.LONG_NAMES: One Intl formatter per zone for its long name, the only place Intl says whether an instant is daylight saving time; Python's tzinfo answers dst().
typescript_only.POSIX_STANDARD: Reads a POSIX TZ string's standard name, against which Intl's reading of the zone is matched; Python's PosixZone answers dst().
typescript_only.SEASON_READINGS: The offsets read around an instant for a zone Intl names only by offset; Python's tzinfo answers dst() for every zone.
typescript_only.daylightName: Whether ICU counts an instant as daylight saving time, read off the zone's long name; Python reads tzinfo's dst().

python_only.YEAR_TEXT: A Python datetime holds no year past 9999, so git's dates past it render whole 400-year cycles earlier and the directives that print a year add the years back; a JavaScript Date holds those years itself.
python_only.year_text: Renders %F, %c and the year directives with the years a datetime past 9999 was moved back; a JavaScript Date needs no such step.
python_only.year_value: The number a year directive shows once those years are added back; a JavaScript Date reads it from the date.

typescript_only.servingMount: Reads the mount a command's files were said to run in (Files.servedBy) before the async context, which the browser's fallback storage does not isolate between tasks; Python's task context always isolates, so crosses_mounts and mount_root read it directly.

python_only.ByteReader: Python stream readers and asyncssh implement readexactly; TypeScript transports expose Web ReadableStreams.

typescript_only.findGeneric: TypeScript's find hands its walk to findGeneric as a find callback; Python's builder calls find_walk_generic, which walks directly.
typescript_only.withRootRow: findGeneric swaps the find callback's row for the start point with its own; Python's find_walk_generic gets the start point's row from the walk.
typescript_only.applyMtimeFilter: findGeneric filters the find callback's rows by overlay mtime; Python's find_walk_generic walks with the overlay stat, so the walk applies -mtime itself.
typescript_only.rowMtime: Asks the overlay mtime of one find-callback row for findGeneric's prune settling; Python's walk reads it off the stat it already has.
typescript_only.rowSpec: Builds the stat probe's path for one find-callback row in findGeneric; Python's walk stats PathSpecs it already holds.

typescript_only.settlePendingPrunes: findGeneric settles the prunes its find callback left pending by asking each directory's mtime; Python's walk settles them inside walk_find through settle_prunes.

typescript_only.keyTexts: A TypeScript driver's key value need not be exact (pg-types parses a jsonb number as a double, and a browser mount takes any driver), so a TypeScript keyset page starts after the key's text form; asyncpg's values are exact, so Python pages from the row itself.

typescript_only.TEXT_PROBE: A browser mount takes any driver, so TypeScript asks whether its driver reads date and time types as Postgres text before a LIKE over their cast; Python's one driver always does (read_as_text in accessor/postgres.py).

python_only._handed_on: Python passes a wrapped backend function the stats and the index its signature names; TypeScript passes them where the function takes its index, as each VFS declares in `handed`.
python_only._takes_index: Python reads whether a backend function takes the index off its signature; a TypeScript VFS declares `index` for it in `handed`.
python_only._wants: Python reads the stats a backend function takes off its parameter names; a TypeScript VFS declares them by method in `handed`, which the mount's `wants` reads.

typescript_only.handedOf: TypeScript carries a call's handed stats in its keyword bag and reads them off it; Python passes them to the backend function as keywords.

typescript_only.digestHeader: Encodes the async WebCrypto digest; Python hashlib/base64 runs inline.

typescript_only.createStore: Node and browser install host-specific scratch storage; Python owns tempfile directly.
typescript_only.factory: Installed host scratch factory; Python uses stdlib tempfile.
typescript_only.setSpoolFactory: Installs Node/browser scratch storage without importing host APIs in core.
typescript_only.SpoolFactory: Typed host scratch factory; Python uses stdlib tempfile directly.
typescript_only.SpoolStore: Host scratch storage interface; Python uses a BinaryIO tempfile.

typescript_only.callerFilesOf: TypeScript has no package-private: Files assigns it from its static block so withCaller reaches the private forCaller.
typescript_only.operandsOfFiles: TypeScript has no package-private: Files assigns it from its static block so operandsOf reaches the private follow; Python's operands_of reads it directly.
typescript_only.pathModeOfFiles: TypeScript has no package-private: Files assigns it from its static block so pathMode reaches the private bind and reader; Python's path_mode reads them directly.
typescript_only.readerOfFiles: TypeScript has no package-private: Files assigns it from its static block so readerOf reaches the private reader; Python's reader_of calls it directly.
typescript_only.withCaller: The door to the private forCaller for the file tool and explain.vfs; Python's task context carries the caller instead, so it has no counterpart.

python_only.shell_line: Python SDK accepts argv or a shell command; this converts that input to a line. The JavaScript SDK passes a command string directly.

typescript_only.Line: Tracks promise completion and cancellation for the JavaScript SDK. Python keeps asyncio Tasks and uses the SDK BaseSandboxSession.
typescript_only.LineOutcome: Local promise-result shape; Python uses the SDK ExecResult type.
typescript_only.errorText: JavaScript catch values are unknown and need conversion to a message; Python uses str(exception).
typescript_only.isSdkDefaultManifest: Recognizes the JavaScript SDK default Manifest fields before selecting the Mirage root; the Python SDK creates its own session state.
typescript_only.mirageManifest: Adapts the JavaScript SDK default manifest root while preserving user manifests; Python uses its SDK session-state creation path.
typescript_only.settleWithin: Promise timeout helper with timer cleanup; Python uses asyncio task waiting.

typescript_only.owned: Wasm streams require explicit handle disposal after final progress; Python releases native state with object ownership.

typescript_only.SEALED: Marks buffers a producer never writes again, so the pipe keeps them instead of copying; Python pipes hold immutable bytes and never copy.

python_only.InlineAwait: asyncio awaits a coroutine in another context, or lets another task cancel it, only through a task of its own, which costs two turns of the event loop per stream pull; TypeScript replays its context in a closure and awaits the promise directly.

python_only.YIELD_SWITCHES: Python yields every few GIL switch intervals, since a loop that yields more often keeps its other threads from the GIL; TypeScript runs every workspace on one thread and keeps a fixed YIELD_INTERVAL.
python_only._TASK_BUDGETS: The budget task_turn keeps per asyncio task; TypeScript has no task identity, so guardDispatch and treeWalk each own a budget per command.
python_only.task_turn: Spends the running asyncio task's budget at the dispatcher, where a command's ops meet; TypeScript has no task identity, so guardDispatch and treeWalk each own a budget per command.

typescript_only.YIELD_INTERVAL: TypeScript has no GIL and yields on a fixed interval; Python derives its interval from the GIL switch interval (YIELD_SWITCHES).

python_only.on_loop: A hosted Python workspace runs on its runner's own event loop thread while the server's transports live on the server's, so work hops between the two; a JavaScript process has one event loop and nothing to hop between.
python_only.owned_task: asyncio starts a task a turn of the loop later and settles it through shield's callbacks, so owned work that never waits would still cost turns; Python 3.12 starts it eagerly. A TypeScript promise starts at once and an await that is already settled takes no turn.

typescript_only.byValue: The compiled-matcher map behind admissionMatcher and visibilityMatcher, keyed by configuration; Python's functools.lru_cache holds the same entries.
typescript_only.cached: Looks a matcher up by its configuration, least recently asked dropped first; Python's functools.lru_cache does the same over the frozen value.

typescript_only.PathsReply: Names the JSON reply shape a profile compile or restriction answers, which TypeScript reads typed; Python reads the same JSON as mappings.
typescript_only.PlanReply: Names the JSON reply shape a profile compile or restriction answers, which TypeScript reads typed; Python reads the same JSON as mappings.
typescript_only.ProfileReply: Names the JSON reply shape a profile compile or restriction answers, which TypeScript reads typed; Python reads the same JSON as mappings.

typescript_only.RulesReply: Names the JSON reply shape a profile compile or restriction answers, which TypeScript reads typed; Python reads the same JSON as mappings.

typescript_only.WIRE_FIELDS: A command_limits entry spells each Limit field in snake_case; pydantic validates and dumps those names itself, a TypeScript Limit takes camelCase, so the config reader and writer map them here.
